segments.en: Well, the details of the job are the specific points about the job.
segments.zh: 好吧，工作的细节是关于工作的具体要点。

segments.en: So for example, if she applied for a job as a receptionist, the details of the job would be answering the phones, taking messages, receiving people at the office.

segments.en: That means behind.
This usually means a person's history at a job or at many jobs or even their educational background, information about where they studied.
segments.zh: 这通常意味着一个人在工作或许多工作中的历史，甚至他们的教育背景，关于他们在哪里学习的信息。

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: And usually you send your resume before you go for the interview so that the employer can look and see is this person qualified, how old are they, what's their work history.
segments.zh: 通常你在去面试之前发送你的简历，这样雇主就可以看看这个人是否有资格，他们多大了，他们的工作经历是什么。

segments.en: Exactly.

Thank you.
Black, no sugar.
No problem.
Sally, can we have two coffees, please?
segments.zh: 莎莉，我们可以喝两杯咖啡吗？

segments.en: One, no milk or sugar.
Certainly, Mr. Parsons.
So Rebecca, I understand you had a first interview with Ms. Childs last week?
segments.zh: 丽贝卡，我了解到你上周已经和柴尔兹女士进行过初面了？

segments.en: Yes, that's correct.
She filled me in on the details of the job on the telephone.
segments.zh: 她在电话中向我介绍了工作的细节。

segments.en: Great.
Well, I'm glad to say she recommended you for a second interview and here we are.
segments.zh: 很高兴告诉你，她推荐你参加第二轮面试，所以今天我们就见面了。

segments.en: Perhaps we can start by discussing your background and resume details a little.
segments.zh: 也许我们可以从讨论您的背景和简历细节开始。

segments.en: Yes, of course.
Alright, so as we mentioned, this is the first part of a ten-part series of the interview series and this is going to be very, very helpful.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如我们提到的，这是面试系列十集中的第一集，会非常非常有用。

segments.en: As you saw in this first part, we're just taking a look at some basic vocab and phrases that you can use when you're just introducing yourself, you're just getting started in the interview.
segments.zh: 正如你在第一部分看到的，我们只是在看一些基础词汇和短语，你可以在自我介绍、刚开始面试时使用。

segments.en: So, what we're going to be looking at later on is talking about yourself, answering questions, but many people don't realize that one of the most important parts of the interview is the very, very beginning because some psychologists say that we make a decision about a person or how we like a person within the first, I think, what, 30 seconds of talking to them?
segments.zh: 所以，我们稍后要看的是谈论你自己、回答问题，但很多人没有意识到，面试中最重要的部分之一就是最开始的时候，因为一些心理学家说，我们在和一个人交谈的头——我想想，多久——30 秒内就会对这个人做出判断，或者决定是否喜欢他。

segments.en: I think so, yeah.
So, it's important that you speak confidently and that you speak, say some of these English phrases comfortably.
segments.zh: 所以，重要的是你要自信地说话，并且能自如地说出这些英语短语。

segments.en: It's a pleasure to meet you.
Oh, it's the pleasure is mine.
These little things will really help you.
segments.zh: 这些小事真的会帮助你。

segments.en: That's right.
And I think as talking about introductions and how this woman arrived to the office, I think one of the key things that we would recommend is to look that person in the eye and give a firm handshake.
segments.zh: 我认为在谈论介绍以及这个女人如何到达办公室时，我认为我们推荐的关键之一是看着那个人的眼睛并坚定地握手。

segments.en: I don't know how many people actually realize how important this is.
segments.zh: 我不知道有多少人真正意识到这有多重要。

segments.en: It's very, very important because as an interviewer, the person or the manager who's interviewing you, I think you can tell a lot from a person if somebody gives you a very flimsy handshake or doesn't look you in the eye.
segments.zh: 这非常非常重要，因为作为面试官、面试你的人或经理，我认为如果有人给你一个非常脆弱的握手或没有看你的眼睛，你可以从一个人那里分辨出很多东西。

segments.en: That's right.
Well, I think in many ways people think, oh, this person is not confident or this person is uncomfortable or this person is hiding something.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为人们在很多方面都在想，哦，这个人不自信，或者这个人不舒服，或者这个人在隐瞒什么。

segments.en: And so, it's important really to be yourself, to smile, to look at a person in the eyes, especially in a lot of like American companies or Canadian companies.
segments.zh: 因此，做你自己、微笑、看着一个人的眼睛很重要，尤其是在很多美国公司或加拿大公司。

segments.en: I know in other parts of the world, smiling with a stranger is unusual or maybe unacceptable, but in America it means I'm confident.
segments.zh: 我知道在世界其他地方，和陌生人微笑是不寻常的，或者可能是不可接受的，但在美国，这意味着我很自信。

segments.en: Here I am.
Here's my name.
Nice to meet you.
It's a very important part of an introduction.
segments.zh: 这是介绍的一个非常重要的部分。

segments.en: Yes, very true.
So we actually want to hear what you think.
segments.zh: 所以我们真的想听听你的想法。

segments.en: How important for you is a handshake, a firm handshake, looking someone in the eye or how do interviews work in your country?
segments.zh: 握手、坚定的握手、直视某人的眼睛或您的国家的面试如何运作对您来说有多重要？

segments.en: Let us know and we hope that this is helpful for you in the future if you're looking for jobs or you just want to practice your English.
segments.zh: 让我们知道，我们希望如果您正在寻找工作或只是想练习英语，这对您将来有所帮助。

segments.en: That's right.
So, if you have any other questions or doubts, we're at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有任何其他问题或疑问，我们在 englishpod.com 上。

segments.en: We'll see everyone there.
Bye.
Bye.
